CHARS_PER_TOKEN = 3


def budget_chars(input_soft, share):
    """Characters a producer may hand a model whose usable window is
    `input_soft` tokens (the catalog row, cut by the curator), for a section
    that takes `share` of that window. None when no window is known: the
    producer then delivers its content whole."""
    try:
        soft = int(float(input_soft))
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return None
    if soft <= 0:
        return None
    return int(soft * share * CHARS_PER_TOKEN)


def clip(text, limit, hint="budget of the window"):
    """`text` whole when it fits `limit` (None: no limit); else its head and
    a mark naming what was shown, the total and how to get the rest."""
    text = "" if text is None else str(text)
    if limit is None or len(text) <= limit:
        return text
    limit = max(0, int(limit))
    return text[:limit] + "...[cut: %d of %d chars shown; %s]" % (
        limit, len(text), hint)

# THE AUDIENCE GATE (GH #925). Every row of `wall`, `calls`, `marks`,
# `summaries` and `pins` carries the audience of the round that caused it
# (`audience_set`, a canonical JSON array), and a reader hands a row to a round
# iff the row has one and it names `*` or holds the round as a subset -- the
# affinity rule (templates/affinity/README.md, GH #154/#306). The round is
# `context.audience_set` of the message being served: this hive's edges set
# and delete only `cur_*`, so it rides the context through every ledger round
# trip exactly like `cur_origin`, and it is never guessed from a row. These
# functions are the same text in every cell of this hive that writes or reads
# rows; a lock holds them to one table. Every ledger read asks the store
# first (`round_where`, GH #932), so a hidden row never comes back at all; the
# Python gate stays as the second line behind it.


def audience_of(value):
    """An audience in its canonical form -- a JSON array of strings, sorted,
    no duplicates, no whitespace -- or None when there is none. The round
    arrives as TEXT (a JSON array in a string) and a column comes back as
    text; a list is taken as it is. Absent, empty text, a scalar or
    unparsable text is NOT DECLARED: the empty list is a declared round, None
    is no round at all (affinity `as_set`, GH #306)."""
    if isinstance(value, str):
        if not value.strip():
            return None
        try:
            value = json.loads(value)
        except ValueError:
            return None
    if not isinstance(value, list):
        return None
    return json.dumps(sorted({str(x) for x in value if str(x)}), separators=(",", ":"))


def allowed(round_value, origin):
    """The gate: a row whose audience is `origin` may reach the round
    `round_value` iff both are declared and the origin names `*` or holds the
    round as a subset. A row from before the rule has no origin and never
    leaves (OR-BD-5); a round nobody declared passes nothing."""
    r, o = audience_of(round_value), audience_of(origin)
    if r is None or o is None:
        return False
    o = set(json.loads(o))
    return "*" in o or set(json.loads(r)) <= o


def passes(row, round_value, session):
    """One reader's verdict on one row. With a declared round it is the gate;
    without one, only a row of the running session that declares no round
    either (or names `*`) passes -- the window and the handover keep a
    round-less conversation going and show nothing from elsewhere (OR-BD-4).
    A row of a declared round never reaches a call nobody declared a round
    for, though it stands in the same session (review M-7: the words of {e,b}
    reached a round-less call of that session, and a round-less recall took
    the addendum of an {e,a} gap). A row that names no session never passes
    a round-less read."""
    if audience_of(round_value) is None:
        if not session or str(row.get("session_id") or "") != session:
            return False
        own = audience_of(row.get("audience_set"))
        return own is not None and (own == "[]" or "*" in json.loads(own))
    return allowed(round_value, row.get("audience_set"))


ROUNDLESS = ["[]", "[\"*\"]"]


def round_where(round_value, session):
    """The store half of the audience gate (GH #932): the `where` terms a
    ledger read adds so that only rows this round may see come back -- page
    bounds, `scanned`, window and renewal sizes and turn counts then hang on
    visible rows alone, and a hidden row costs nothing a reader can count.
    With a declared, non-empty round it is `covers` (the affinity rule in the
    store). Without one -- or with a declared EMPTY round, which `covers`
    refuses -- only rows of the running session that declare no round either
    (`[]`, PP-BD-12) or name `*` come back; a row from before the rule (NULL)
    never does. None: nothing may be read at all (no round and no session).
    The Python gate below stays as the second line."""
    r = audience_of(round_value)
    if r is not None and r != "[]":
        return {"audience_set": {"covers": json.loads(r)}}
    if not session:
        return None
    return {"session_id": session, "audience_set": {"in": list(ROUNDLESS)}}


def audience_meet(values):
    """The audience of a row made of other rows (a summary, a handover
    block): the INTERSECTION of its sources, so it can never be wider than
    any of them (OR-BD-3). A source naming `*` is neutral; one source without
    an audience, or no source at all, makes the result None."""
    out, universal = None, False
    for v in values:
        c = audience_of(v)
        if c is None:
            return None
        s = set(json.loads(c))
        if "*" in s:
            universal = True
            continue
        out = s if out is None else out & s
    if out is None:
        return '["*"]' if universal else None
    return json.dumps(sorted(out), separators=(",", ":"))

def held(kind, key):
    """Whether a message of this child still in flight holds `key` (A1): the
    guard against a twin racing it -- never the record of a write."""
    return any(key in keys for keys in _MEM[kind].values())


def hold(kind, call, keys):
    """`keys` held under `call` until the store answers its write (A1)."""
    _MEM[kind].setdefault(call, set()).update(keys)


def release(call):
    """Everything held under `call`: its write was answered -- landed or
    refused, the ledger decides from here (A1)."""
    for kind in ("delivered", "used"):
        _MEM[kind].pop(call, None)


def canonical(value):
    """The one serialisation a block is hashed and stored in: keys sorted,
    UTF-8, no whitespace."""
    return json.dumps(value, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False)


def block_hash(value):
    return hashlib.sha256(canonical(value).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()


def block_span(text):
    """Where an answer's sidecar block stands: (start, end) or None.

    The boundary is the fence `talky/splitter` cuts (GH #379, #605): the
    ```sidecar fence, or the legacy ```memory fence, to the next closing fence
    or to the end of the text when the completion stopped inside the block.
    Measured, never parsed -- the sections inside are somebody else's business.
    """
    low = text.lower()
    for fence in ("```sidecar", "```memory"):
        at = low.find(fence)
        if at < 0:
            continue
        head = text.find("\n", at)
        close = text.find("```", head + 1) if head >= 0 else -1
        if head >= 0 and close >= 0:
            return at, close + 3
        return at, len(text)
    return None


def stripped_text(text):
    span = block_span(text)
    if span is None:
        return text
    return (text[:span[0]] + text[span[1]:]).strip()

def lstore(ops, phase, call="", reason=""):

                       "cur_call": call, "cur_reason": reason},
            "messages": [{"origin": "assistant", "type": "tool_call", "id": cid,

def legs(body):
    """The answer of a store message by tool_call id: payload, error code and
    rows affected -- for a bundle (`results[]`) and for a single op alike."""
    out = {}
    for m in body.get("messages") or []:
        if not isinstance(m, dict):
            continue
        try:
            payload = json.loads(m.get("text") or "null")
        except Exception:
            payload = None
        out[str(m.get("id") or "")] = {"payload": payload, "error_code": "",
                                       "rows_affected": 0}
    results = body.get("results")
    if isinstance(results, list):
        for r in results:
            if not isinstance(r, dict):
                continue
            leg = out.setdefault(str(r.get("tool_call_id") or ""),
                                 {"payload": None, "error_code": "", "rows_affected": 0})
            leg["error_code"] = str(r.get("error_code") or "")
            leg["rows_affected"] = int(r.get("rows_affected") or 0)
    elif len(out) == 1:
        leg = next(iter(out.values()))
        leg["error_code"] = str(hop.get("error_code") or "")
        leg["rows_affected"] = int(hop.get("rows_affected") or 0)
    return out


def rows(lg, cid):

def stamped(row, audience, meet=False):
    """A `marks` row with the audience it was caused under (GH #925). A
    round nobody declared writes `[]` (PP-BD-12): a round-less row the
    round-less reads of its own session find in the store (`round_where`),
    where a NULL column would be a row from before the rule that no reader
    hands on (OR-BD-5)."""
    if audience is not None:
        row["audience_set"] = audience
    elif not meet:
        row["audience_set"] = "[]"

    # column stays NULL, a row no reader hands on -- never `[]`, which a
    # round-less read of the session would take.

def addendum_audience(round_value, gap_audience):
    """The audience of an addendum (OR-BD-3): the meet of the gap's round and
    the round its find came home in. Both round-less (`[]`, PP-BD-12; or the
    gap names `*`) is a round-less addendum, `[]`. One side round-less and the
    other a declared round, or two rounds that share nobody, is NOT a
    round-less row -- it would reach the round-less reads of the session --
    but one nobody may be shown: None."""
    r, g = audience_of(round_value), audience_of(gap_audience)
    if r in (None, "[]"):
        return "[]" if g in ("[]", '["*"]') else None
    if g == "[]":

    return None if out == "[]" else out


def round_read(cid, table, columns, where, order=None, limit=None, session=None):

    (no round and no session), so the reader finds no rows without a store
    call."""
    rw = round_where(ROUND, session)
    if rw is None:
        return []
    return [(cid, sel(table, columns, dict(where or {}, **rw), order, limit))]


def visible(found, session):

    asked with (`passes`, GH #925, OR-BD.A.2): with a round, the gate; without
    one, the running session only. A hidden row leaves no trace. The read
    itself already asked the store (`round_read`, GH #932); this is the

    return [r for r in found if isinstance(r, dict) and passes(r, ROUND, session)]


def value_of(row):

def knob_on(value):

    and "no" are off -- and so is a flag nobody stamped."""
    if isinstance(value, bool):
        return value
    return str(value if value is not None else "").strip().lower() not in (

def knob_budget(value):

        return DEFAULT_BUDGET

def query_budget(budget, soft, fixed=False):
    """GH #1040: the question's budget for an asker with `soft` tokens of
    `input_soft`: the role's preset times the growth of the memory hive's
    query guard, unchanged without a package or for a budget the instance set
    itself (`fixed`)."""
    try:
        soft = int(float(soft))
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        soft = 0
    if fixed or soft <= 0 or budget <= 0:
        return budget
    grow = min(max(1.0, soft * QUERY_SHARE / QUERY_BASE_TOKENS), QUERY_GROWTH_MAX)
    return int(budget * grow + 0.5)


def the_ask(h, body):

def topic_of(marks):
    """The open topic of this session (OR-KY-71): the name of the newest topic
    mark that carries one, unless an `end` came after it. `./intake` writes a
    mark as the canonical JSON of the memory section's `{movement, name}`; a
    bare string is a movement and names nothing."""
    for r in marks:
        v = value_of(r)
        if isinstance(v, dict):
            movement = str(v.get("movement") or "").strip().lower()
            name = str(v.get("name") or "").strip()
        else:
            movement, name = str(v or "").strip().lower(), ""
        if movement == "end":
            return ""
        if name:
            return name
    return ""


def recent_rounds(wall):
    """The participant rows of the newest `ENTITY_ROUNDS` rounds of the wall
    (newest first): the person's and a peer's turns and the model's final
    answers -- an interim sentence beside a tool call says nothing new."""
    keys, out = [], []
    for r in wall:
        key = (str(r.get("session_id") or ""), str(r.get("turn_id") or ""))
        kind = str(r.get("kind") or "")
        if kind == "assistant" and int(r.get("final") or 0) != 1:
            continue
        if kind not in ("user", "peer", "assistant"):
            continue
        if key not in keys:
            if len(keys) >= ENTITY_ROUNDS:
                break
            keys.append(key)
        out.append(r)
    return out


def known_hits(text, known):
    """The spellings the round already knows as names (`known`, GH #1225 B4)
    that stand in `text` as whole words, in the order they stand there."""
    out = []
    for k in known:
        m = re.search(r"(?<!\w)%s(?!\w)" % re.escape(k), text, re.IGNORECASE | re.UNICODE)
        if m:
            out.append((m.start(), k))
    return [k for _, k in sorted(out)]


def entities(texts, skip, known=()):
    """The fixed heuristic of R-27-11 A (OR-KY-P1), made a list of names
    (GH #1225 B4): in each text, first the spellings the round already knows
    as names (`known`), then in order quotes, dates, numbers, and words that
    start with a capital where no sentence starts -- none a word of
    `ENTITY_STOP` and none a noun by its form unless a salutation, a title or
    a kinship word -- a capital word of `ENTITY_STOP` that is no determiner
    (`ENTITY_DET`) -- stands right in front of it: what follows one is a name
    whatever its form ("Herrn Hartung", "Tochter Anna"); a weekday or a month
    (`ENTITY_DATE`) is a date wherever it stands. Newest text first, in the
    order they stand, each once, at most `ENTITY_MAX`, none the person
    already said. Nothing here guesses a name: a list says what is not one."""
    seen, out = set(skip), []
    if ENTITY_MAX <= 0:
        return out
    for text in texts:
        for k in known_hits(text, known):
            parts = [w.lower() for w in re.findall(r"\w+", k)]
            if k.lower() in seen or not parts or all(w in seen for w in parts):
                continue
            seen.add(k.lower())
            seen.update(parts)
            out.append(k)
            if len(out) >= ENTITY_MAX:
                return out
        prev = None
        before = []
        for m in TOKEN.finditer(text):
            quoted = next((g for g in m.groups()[:4] if g), None)
            date, number, word = m.group(5), m.group(6), m.group(7)
            # A sentence starts at the text's first token and after a stop or
            # a line break -- what lies BETWEEN two tokens says so.
            at_start = prev is None or bool(SENTENCE_GAP.search(text[prev:m.start()]))
            prev = m.end()
            if at_start:
                before = []
            item = ""
            if quoted:
                item = quoted.strip()
            elif date:
                item = date
            elif number:
                item = number
            elif word and word[0].isupper():
                name = POSSESSIVE.sub("", word).rstrip("-'’")
                low = unicodedata.normalize("NFC", name).casefold()
                if low in ENTITY_DATE:
                    item = name
                elif not at_start and len(name) >= 2 and low not in ENTITY_STOP \
                        and not low.startswith("i'"):
                    lead = unicodedata.normalize("NFC", before[-1]).casefold() if before else ""
                    titled = before[-1][:1].isupper() and lead in ENTITY_STOP \
                        and lead not in ENTITY_DET if before else False
                    if titled or not a_noun_by_form(low):
                        item = name
            if word:
                before.append(word)
            if not item or item.lower() in seen:
                continue
            seen.add(item.lower())
            out.append(item)
            if len(out) >= ENTITY_MAX:
                return out
    return out


def compose(user_text, topic, found, refs, budget):
    """The query: what the wall knows, in front of the person's own words, and
    never more than `budget` characters. The person's words are never cut --
    the memory hive's own hygiene guard is the one place a question is cut
    (GH #88) -- and they come LAST, because that guard and its keyword cap
    both keep the tail of a query."""
    parts = []
    if topic:
        parts.append("topic: " + topic)
    if found:
        parts.append("mentioned: " + ", ".join(found))
    for r in refs:
        parts.append("refers to: " + r)
    if budget <= 0 or len(user_text) >= budget:
        return user_text
    room = budget - len(user_text) - 1
    kept = []
    for p in parts:
        piece = "; ".join(kept + [p])
        if len(piece) + 2 > room:
            if p.startswith("mentioned: "):
                # Fewer entities rather than none: drop from the oldest end.
                names = list(found)
                while names:
                    names.pop()
                    trial = "; ".join(kept + ["mentioned: " + ", ".join(names)])
                    if names and len(trial) + 2 <= room:
                        kept.append("mentioned: " + ", ".join(names))
                        break
            continue
        kept.append(p)
    if not kept:
        return user_text
    return "[" + "; ".join(kept) + "] " + user_text


def element_text(body):
    try:
        el = json.loads(str(body or ""))
    except ValueError:
        return ""
    return str(el.get("text") or "") if isinstance(el, dict) else ""


# ------------------------------------------------------------ the addendum

def addendum_pair(gap, text):
    """The pair a find is shown as (OR-KY-P3): a `memory_recall` call with the
    gap as its question and the find as its result, framed as an addendum.
    The id is derived, so the same find for the same gap is the same pair --
    the same hash, and a pair the window already carries is not carried twice."""
    cid = "call_addendum_" + hashlib.sha256(
        ("%s\x1f%s" % (gap, text)).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:16]
    call = {"origin": "assistant", "type": "tool_call", "id": cid,
            "text": json.dumps({"name": RECALL_TOOL,
                                "arguments": json.dumps({"query": gap})})}
    result = {"origin": "tool", "type": "tool_result", "id": cid,
              "text": (ADDENDUM_FRAME % gap) + "\n" + text}
    return call, result


def candidate_pair(part, triggers, session, turn):
    """The pair the candidates of one turn are shown as (GH #949, OR-BC.K.2):
    a `memory_recall` call whose `query` is the triggers the person's words
    hit -- each once, by the form they match in (`tokens_of`), joined with
    ", "; "" when none carried a trigger -- and a result that is
    `CANDIDATE_FRAME` and the part. The triggers ride beside the part rather
    than inside its id: the id is derived from (session, turn, part) alone,
    so a twin of the same ask maps onto the same pair (the wall's key keeps
    it once) while every showing in another turn is a pair of its own -- a
    cooldown that lets a candidate come back means it is shown again."""
    said, forms = [], set()
    for t in triggers or []:
        form = " ".join(tokens_of(t))
        if form and form not in forms:
            forms.add(form)
            said.append(str(t))
    cid = "call_candidates_" + hashlib.sha256(
        ("%s\x1f%s\x1f%s" % (session, turn, part)).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:16]
    call = {"origin": "assistant", "type": "tool_call", "id": cid,
            "text": json.dumps({"name": RECALL_TOOL,
                                "arguments": json.dumps({"query": ", ".join(said)})})}
    result = {"origin": "tool", "type": "tool_result", "id": cid,
              "text": CANDIDATE_FRAME + "\n" + part}
    return call, result


def bundle_find(body, h):
    """The readable text of a gap's bundle, or "" when memory had nothing: an
    empty bundle says so on its hop (`recall_empty`, #297), a refusal comes as
    a reject (`reject_reason`), and the empty-state sentence is not a find."""
    if str(h.get("recall_empty") or "") == "1" or str(h.get("reject_reason") or ""):
        return ""
    text = ""
    for m in body.get("messages") or []:
        if isinstance(m, dict) and str(m.get("text") or "").strip():
            text = str(m.get("text") or "").strip()
    if not text or text.startswith(NOTHING_PREFIX):
        return ""
    return text


def unmarked(text):
    """`text` without the short block ids it quotes, in the splitter's form
    (GH #894): an id at the very start takes the space behind it along."""
    out = SPOKEN_ID.sub("", text)
    if out == text:
        return text
    return out.lstrip(" \t") if SPOKEN_ID.match(text) else out


def with_soft(header, soft):
    """`header` with the window as it leaves on every ask (R-IG-1, GH #1085):
    `input_soft`, the tokens of the usable window as a number, and no key at
    all when none is known. `recall_input_soft` stays beside it, the same
    value as a string, "" for none (its alias, GH #1040)."""
    header["recall_input_soft"] = soft
    try:
        n = int(float(soft))
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        n = 0
    if n > 0:
        header["input_soft"] = n
    else:
        header.pop("input_soft", None)
    return header


def said_aloud(gap, text):
    """A find as the voice model hears it: one plain paragraph, and no short
    block id in it. The `fact` leaves the colony -- the member hands it to the
    channel as advice and the voice reads it out -- and R-27-3 keeps internal
    ids inside (OR-KY-68). Both halves can carry one: the gap section passes
    the splitter's filter on purpose (the curator's sections keep their ids),
    and a model with `short_ids` on writes "whether [#0123456789ab] ..." there;
    a find quotes episodes of earlier answers as the tap filed them. The
    window's addendum keeps the ids: the model reads it, and `history_read`
    takes them (review I-2)."""
    flat = unmarked(" ".join(line.strip(" -*\t") for line in text.splitlines()
                             if line.strip()))
    return "Addendum to what was just said (%s): %s" % (unmarked(gap), flat)


# ------------------------------------------------------------ the candidates

def candidate_where(round_value):
    """The `where` of the candidates read (GH #949): the store half of the
    audience gate for a table that names no session -- the rule `./policy`
    `rebuild_where` reads its rows by. A declared, non-empty round is `covers`
    (the round never widens: a row is read only if it names `*` or holds the
    whole round); none, or the declared EMPTY round `covers` refuses, reads
    only the rows that declare no round (`[]`) or name `*`, and never a row
    from before the rule (NULL)."""
    r = audience_of(round_value)
    if r is not None and r != "[]":
        return {"audience_set": {"covers": json.loads(r)}}
    return {"audience_set": {"in": list(ROUNDLESS)}}


def candidate_passes(row, round_value):
    """The second line behind `candidate_where`: the same rule over one row.
    A row without an audience reaches no round; a round-less ask (or the
    empty round) takes only `[]` and `*`."""
    own = audience_of(row.get("audience_set"))
    if own is None:
        return False
    r = audience_of(round_value)
    if r is None or r == "[]":
        return own in ROUNDLESS
    return allowed(r, own)


def candidate_live(row, as_of):
    """Whether a candidate may be shown at `as_of` (an aware datetime): its
    `until` empty or still ahead, and a `once` candidate not yet used. An
    `until` that does not read as a time ends it -- fail-closed, the door
    (`./intake`) refuses such a row anyway."""
    if str(row.get("once") or "0").strip() not in ("", "0") and str(row.get("used_at") or "").strip():
        return False
    u = str(row.get("until") or "").strip()
    if not u:
        return True
    try:
        t = datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(u.replace("Z", "+00:00"))
    except ValueError:
        return False
    if t.tzinfo is None:
        t = t.replace(tzinfo=datetime.timezone.utc)
    return t > as_of


def match_form(token):
    """One token as a trigger is compared in: NFC, casefolded (NFC again --
    a casefold may decompose), without a possessive `'s` and without a
    trailing hyphen, apostrophe or dot (a date the sentence ends on keeps
    its dot in the token rule)."""
    t = unicodedata.normalize("NFC", unicodedata.normalize("NFC", token).casefold())
    return POSSESSIVE.sub("", t).rstrip("-'’.")


def tokens_of(text):
    """The tokens of a text as triggers match them: `CANDIDATE_TOKEN` over the
    text in NFC -- a decomposed accent is no word character and would cut a
    word in two -- each in its `match_form`."""
    flat = unicodedata.normalize("NFC", str(text or ""))
    out = []
    for m in CANDIDATE_TOKEN.finditer(flat):
        t = match_form(m.group(0))
        if t:
            out.append(t)
    return out


def trigger_hits(trigger, turn_tokens):
    """Whether `trigger` stands in a turn whose tokens are `turn_tokens`
    (`tokens_of`): its tokens as a run of consecutive tokens of the turn,
    whole tokens only -- `firewalls` is no `firewall`, `Xenon` no `X`. A
    trigger without a token (punctuation only) hits nothing."""
    want = tokens_of(trigger)
    n = len(want)
    if not n:
        return False
    return any(turn_tokens[i:i + n] == want for i in range(len(turn_tokens) - n + 1))


def triggers_of(row):
    """A candidate's triggers as the door stored them (a JSON list of
    strings): [] for none -- shown on every turn -- and None for a column
    that does not read as such a list, which nothing ever hits
    (fail-closed: a broken trigger must not turn into "always")."""
    raw = row.get("triggers")
    if raw is None or (isinstance(raw, str) and not raw.strip()):
        return []
    try:
        v = json.loads(raw) if isinstance(raw, str) else raw
    except ValueError:
        return None
    if not isinstance(v, list) or not all(isinstance(t, str) for t in v):
        return None
    return v


def turns_since(wall_rows, mark):
    """How many turns of the conversation the round saw after `mark` (a
    `last_seq`): distinct (session, turn) of the person's and a peer's rows
    with a higher `seq`, out of the push's own page of the wall. A page that
    does not reach back that far counts low, so a candidate waits longer,
    never shorter."""
    seen = set()
    for r in wall_rows:
        if str(r.get("kind") or "") not in ("user", "peer"):
            continue
        try:
            if int(r.get("seq") or 0) <= mark:
                continue
        except (TypeError, ValueError):
            continue
        seen.add((str(r.get("session_id") or ""), str(r.get("turn_id") or "")))
    return len(seen)


def pick_candidates(found, round_value, turn_tokens, wall_rows, as_of, cooldown):
    """The candidates this turn may carry, best first -- priority, then the
    youngest (`at`), then source and id for a fixed order: those the round
    may see, live, hit by a trigger of the person's words (or without one),
    and not shown within `cooldown` turns. Each as `{source, id, hash,
    once, hits}` -- `hits` the triggers the words said, in the candidate's
    own order, for the call of its pair (`candidate_pair`); the texts are
    read after, by hash."""
    out = []
    for r in found:
        if not isinstance(r, dict) or not candidate_passes(r, round_value):
            continue
        if not str(r.get("hash") or "") or not candidate_live(r, as_of):
            continue
        trig = triggers_of(r)
        hits = [t for t in trig or [] if trigger_hits(t, turn_tokens)]
        if trig is None or (trig and not hits):
            continue
        try:
            last = int(r.get("last_seq") or 0)
        except (TypeError, ValueError):
            continue
        if last > 0 and cooldown > 0 and turns_since(wall_rows, last) < cooldown:
            continue
        try:
            prio = int(r.get("priority"))
        except (TypeError, ValueError):
            prio = CANDIDATE_PRIORITY
        out.append({"source": str(r.get("source") or ""), "id": str(r.get("cand_id") or ""),
                    "hash": str(r.get("hash") or ""),
                    "once": str(r.get("once") or "0").strip() not in ("", "0"),
                    "hits": hits, "prio": prio, "at": str(r.get("at") or "")})
    out.sort(key=lambda c: (c["source"], c["id"]))
    out.sort(key=lambda c: c["at"], reverse=True)
    out.sort(key=lambda c: c["prio"], reverse=True)
    return [{k: c[k] for k in ("source", "id", "hash", "once", "hits")} for c in out]


def candidate_part(texts, budget):
    """The candidates' part of the result of their pair, `[<text>; <text>]`,
    in the order given and never more than `budget` characters (brackets and
    separators counted; None: every one): whole candidates or none -- one that
    does not fit is left out whole, and a later, shorter one may still fit
    (the rule `compose` cuts its parts by). What is left out is said behind
    the part (R-IG-1), and stays unsaid for a later turn. A text said twice is
    said once. Returns the part and the indices it carries; ("", []) for
    none."""
    kept, idx, left = [], [], []
    for i, t in enumerate(texts):
        if not t:
            continue
        if t in kept:
            idx.append(i)
            continue
        if budget is not None and len("[" + "; ".join(kept + [t]) + "]") > budget:
            if t not in left:
                left.append(t)
            continue
        kept.append(t)
        idx.append(i)
    if not kept:
        return "", []
    part = "[" + "; ".join(kept) + "]"
    if left:
        part += " ...[dropped: %d candidates (%d chars) over budget]" % (
            len(left), sum(len(t) for t in left))
    return part, idx


def candidate_key(c):
    return "%s\x1f%s" % (c.get("source", ""), c.get("id", ""))


# ======================================================================= LANES
# The round this message serves, read here at every step (OR-BD.A.1): the
# context rides every ledger round trip of this hive, and a gap's ask out of
# the hive and its answer home. Never read off a row.
ROUND = ctx.get("audience_set")
AUD = audience_of(ROUND)
lane = str(hop.get("route") or "")
phase = str(ctx.get("cur_phase") or "")
op = str(hop.get("operation") or "")
call = str(ctx.get("cur_call") or "")
reason = str(ctx.get("cur_reason") or "")


def ask_as_it_came(ask, soft, failed):
    """The collector's ask with the window it is sized by -- the fallback
    row's when the read of it failed, never the old sizes in silence -- and
    the reads it lacks named (B6)."""
    with_soft(ask["header"], soft)
    with_degraded(ask["header"], failed)
    return ask


# The values an `addendum_done` can carry besides "shown": its key is the id.
DONE_WHY = ("", "in the window", "its blocks are gone")


def landed(lg, leg):
    """Whether the write `leg` of a ledger answer wrote a row (A1)."""
    a = lg.get(leg) or {}
    return not a.get("error_code") and int(a.get("rows_affected") or 0) >= 1


def said_part(cpart, session, turn, lg=None):
    """The candidates' pair of one turn and the indices it carries: every
    word of `cpart`, a `once` whose update did not land (`lg`) left out."""
    words = list(cpart.get("words") or [])
    if lg is not None:
        for i, leg in (cpart.get("legs") or {}).items():
            if not landed(lg, leg):
                words[int(i)] = ""
    part, idx = candidate_part(words, cpart.get("budget"))
    if part and cpart.get("more"):
        part += (" ...[more: a full page of %d candidate rows was read; the "
                 "rest may come in a later turn]" % int(cpart["more"]))
    if not part:
        return [], []
    hits = cpart.get("hits") or []
    return list(candidate_pair(part, [t for i in idx for t in hits[i]], session, turn)), idx


def shown_of(show, lg):
    """The `in_addendum` message of a turn: the finds' pairs whose mark
    landed and the candidates' pair behind them; none when empty. `lg`
    None: nothing waited for the ledger."""
    pair = []
    for g in show.get("gaps") or []:
        if lg is None or landed(lg, g.get("leg")):
            pair += g.get("msgs") or []
    if show.get("cands"):
        pair += said_part(show["cands"], show["session"], show["turn"], lg)[0]
    return [{"header": {"route": "in_addendum", "session_id": show["session"],
                        "turn_id": show["turn"]}, "messages": pair}] if pair else []


def finish_ask(slim, lg):
    """The second step of an ask (phase `ask-b`, or straight from `ask` when
    it had nothing more to read): the question, the addenda, the candidates
    and the writes they cost. `slim` rides `cur_reason` (B5)."""
    ask = slim["ask"]
    head = ask["header"]
    session = str(head.get("session_id") or "default")
    turn = str(head.get("turn_id") or "")
    text = str(head.get("recall_query") or "")
    failed = list(slim.get("failed") or [])
    # GH #1225 B6: a read that failed is no empty one. Without the blocks
    # there are no texts and no pairs; without the window's rows nothing can
    # say a pair is not in it yet -- both wait, unmarked, for a later ask.
    blocks_err = error_code_of(lg, "b-blocks")
    seen_err = error_code_of(lg, "b-seen")
    if blocks_err:
        failed += ["b-blocks"]
    if seen_err:
        failed += ["b-seen"]
    blocks = {}
    for r in ([] if blocks_err else rows(lg, "b-blocks")):
        blocks.setdefault(str(r.get("hash") or ""), r)
    texts = []
    for r in slim.get("recent") or []:
        b = blocks.get(r.get("hash"))
        if b is not None:
            texts.append(stripped_text(element_text(b.get("body"))))
    found = entities([t for t in texts if t], {w.lower() for w in re.findall(r"\w+", text)},
                     [k for k in slim.get("known") or [] if isinstance(k, str) and k.strip()])
    refs = []
    for i, ref in enumerate(slim.get("refs") or []):
        ref_err = error_code_of(lg, "b-ref%d" % i) or error_code_of(lg, "b-refw%d" % i)
        if ref_err:
            failed += ["b-ref%d" % i]
            continue
        seen_by = {str(r.get("hash") or "") for r in visible(rows(lg, "b-refw%d" % i), session)}
        for r in rows(lg, "b-ref%d" % i):
            h_ = str(r.get("hash") or "")
            if h_.startswith(ref) and h_ in seen_by:
                snip = " ".join(stripped_text(element_text(r.get("body"))).split())
                if snip:
                    # B7: a block longer than REF_CHARS is cut WITH a mark --
                    # one character, because the question is search words.
                    refs.append(snip if len(snip) <= REF_CHARS else snip[:REF_CHARS] + "…")
    soft = str(slim.get("input_soft") or "")
    query = compose(text, str(slim.get("topic") or ""), found, refs,
                    query_budget(int(slim.get("budget") or DEFAULT_BUDGET), soft,
                                 bool(slim.get("fixed"))))
    out = with_query(ask, query)
    with_soft(out["header"], soft)
    with_degraded(out["header"], failed)
    stamp = now()
    ops = []
    # The memory tier the ambient leg of this surface asks with: a gap is
    # looked up at the same tier, and only where an ambient leg exists. One
    # step, never read-then-insert (OR-KF-3); not at all when the read of it
    # failed (B6).
    tier = str(head.get("memory_tier") or "")
    if slim.get("tier_known") and (not slim.get("has_tier") or slim.get("tier") != tier):
        ops.append(("c-tier", ins("state", {"key": "push:tier", "value": tier},
                                  replace={"key": "push:tier"})))
    # Prompt hygiene: the slot is this hive's, written once and again only
    # when its words change -- the block if absent, the slot in one step by
    # its path (UNIQUE `slots(path)`, OR-KF-3); not at all when the read of
    # the slot failed (B6).
    slot = slim.get("slot")
    words = HYGIENE + (HYGIENE_IDS if slim.get("short") else "")
    el = {"path": HYGIENE_PATH, "text": words}
    sh = block_hash(el)
    if slim.get("slot_known") and (not isinstance(slot, dict) or str(slot.get("hash") or "") != sh):
        ops.append(("c-hb", ins("blocks", {"hash": sh, "kind": "system", "chars": len(words),
                                           "body": canonical(el), "first_seen": stamp},
                                if_absent={"hash": sh})))
        ops.append(("c-hs", ins("slots", {"path": HYGIENE_PATH, "hash": sh,
                                          "owner": "curator", "at": stamp},
                                replace={"path": HYGIENE_PATH})))
    # The addenda: for THIS round. The pair goes to `./intake`, the wall's
    # one writer (OR-KX.K.1), only after the ledger answered the write of its
    # `addendum_done` (phase `done`); the ask leaves at once, so the pair and
    # the memory's answer race -- the round's first turn comes in only after
    # the memory answered, and nothing orders the two.
    # A pair whose result the window already carries is not carried twice.
    seen = {str(r.get("hash") or "") for r in visible(rows(lg, "b-seen"), session)}
    pair, rows_out = [], []
    for p in ([] if blocks_err or seen_err else slim.get("pending") or []):
        # A1: a twin of this child already hands it on -- its own mark decides.
        if held("delivered", p["id"]):
            continue
        cb, rb = blocks.get(p["call"]), blocks.get(p["result"])
        why = ""
        if p["result"] in seen:
            why = "in the window"
        elif cb is None or rb is None:
            why = "its blocks are gone"
        else:
            pair.append([json.loads(str(cb.get("body") or "{}")),
                         json.loads(str(rb.get("body") or "{}"))])
        # Two finds of one pair in one round are one block, shown once.
        seen.add(p["result"])
        rows_out.append((p, why, len(pair) - 1 if not why else -1))
    # A1: held only while its `addendum_done` is on its way (phase `done`).
    hold("delivered", call, [p["id"] for p, _, _ in rows_out])
    # GH #949, OR-BC.K.2: the candidates this turn carries, as ONE pair
    # behind the gaps' -- into the window of the model, the one reader
    # they are for. `recall_query` reaches the memory alone (its guard
    # keeps the last sentence of a query over 200 characters) and never
    # the model, so the question above stays as it was. Only a block the
    # door filed as a candidate is said; a `once` another message of this
    # child is handing out is not said twice while its `used_at` is on its
    # way. A turn without an id gets no pair (`./intake` writes none without
    # one), so nothing is marked as said that the wall never got.
    said, words, cpart = [], [], None
    cands = [] if blocks_err else slim.get("cands") or []
    if cands and CANDIDATE_PUSH and turn:
        try:
            for c in cands:
                b = blocks.get(c.get("hash"))
                w = ""
                if b is not None and str(b.get("kind") or "") == "candidate":
                    w = " ".join(element_text(b.get("body")).split())
                if c.get("once") and held("used", candidate_key(c)):
                    w = ""
                words.append(w)
            cpart = {"words": words, "hits": [c.get("hits") or [] for c in cands],
                     "budget": budget_chars(str(slim.get("input_soft") or ""), CANDIDATE_SHARE),
                     "more": int(slim.get("cands_more") or 0), "legs": {}}
            sidx = said_part(cpart, session, turn)[1]
            said = [cands[i] for i in sidx]
        except Exception as exc:
            sys.stderr.write("curator/push: ask %s carries no candidate (%s)\n" % (call, exc))
            said, cpart = [], None
    # A1: `addendum_done` once per find -- written if absent, keyed by the id
    # (every value one can carry), and only the message whose mark landed
    # shows the pair (phase `done`): a twin, in this child or after a restart,
    # neither shows it again nor marks it twice.
    gaps = []
    for (p, why, at), seq in zip(rows_out, next_seq(len(rows_out)) if rows_out else []):
        ops.append(("c-m%d" % seq, ins("marks", stamped({
            "seq": seq, "session_id": session, "turn_id": turn,
            "kind": "addendum_done",
            "value": canonical({"id": p["id"], "delivered": 0 if why else 1,
                                "why": why}), "at": stamp}, AUD),
            if_absent={"session_id": session, "kind": "addendum_done",
                       "value": {"in": [canonical({"id": p["id"], "delivered": 0 if w else 1,
                                                   "why": w}) for w in DONE_WHY]}})))
        if at >= 0:
            gaps.append({"leg": "c-m%d" % seq, "msgs": pair[at]})
    if said:
        # What was said is on the record in the same bundle: `last_seq`
        # is a `seq` of the wall's clock (microseconds, `next_seq`),
        # minted before the person's words of this turn reach the wall,
        # so this turn is the first the cooldown counts; a `once`
        # candidate is used. Keyed by its hash too: a text the source
        # replaced meanwhile was not said and keeps its marks.
        mark_seq = next_seq(1)[0]
        for i, c in enumerate(said):
            vals = {"last_seq": mark_seq}
            where = {"source": c["source"], "cand_id": c["id"], "hash": c["hash"]}
            if c.get("once"):
                # A1: used once -- the update that finds it unused says it.
                vals["used_at"] = stamp
                where["used_at"] = {"or_null": {"eq": ""}}
                hold("used", call, [candidate_key(c)])
                cpart["legs"][str(sidx[i])] = "c-cand%d" % i
            ops.append(("c-cand%d" % i, upd("candidates", vals, where)))
    show = {"session": session, "turn": turn, "gaps": gaps, "cands": cpart}
    if gaps or (cpart and cpart["legs"]):
        # What only a landed write may show waits for the ledger's answer;
        # the ask leaves now -- the question pays no round trip for it.
        shown, reason_done = [], canonical(show)
    else:
        shown, reason_done = shown_of(show, None), ""
    # B6 (c): a find whose marks could not be read is held in the state; the
    # next message of its round -- this one -- looks at it again. No timer.
    again = [lstore([("h-echo", sel("state", ["key", "value"],
                                    {"key": pending_key("gap-" + gid)})),
                     ("h-marks", sel("marks", ["turn_id", "kind", "value", "audience_set"],
                                     {"session_id": session,
                                      "kind": {"in": ["gap", "addendum"]}}))],
                    "hit", "gap-" + gid, canonical({"session": session, "held": 1}))
             for gid in slim.get("holds") or []]
    if not ops:
        release(call)
        return shown + again + [out]
    return [lstore(ops, "done", call, reason_done)] + shown + again + [out]


def keep_find(st, gid, live, now_err=""):
    """The writes of a find (phases `hit` and `keep`): the pair's blocks if
    absent, the `addendum` mark if absent -- the ledger, never this child's
    RAM, says whether it is kept (A1) -- the held find let go. A duplex
    call's `fact` waits for the mark's answer (phase `kept`): said only when
    THIS message kept the find, so a twin is never said twice."""
    c_el, r_el = addendum_pair(st["gap"], st["text"])
    stamp = now()
    ops = []
    for i, (el, h) in enumerate(((c_el, st["call"]), (r_el, st["result"]))):
        ops.append(("k-b%d" % i, ins("blocks", {"hash": h, "kind": "recall",
                                                "chars": len(str(el.get("text") or "")),
                                                "body": canonical(el),
                                                "first_seen": stamp},
                                     if_absent={"hash": h})))
    value = canonical({"id": gid, "call": st["call"], "result": st["result"], "gap": st["gap"]})
    ops.append(("k-mark", ins("marks", stamped({
        "seq": next_seq(1)[0], "session_id": st["session"], "turn_id": st["turn"],
        "kind": "addendum", "value": value, "at": stamp}, st.get("audience"), meet=True),
        if_absent={"session_id": st["session"], "kind": "addendum", "value": value})))
    if st.get("held"):
        ops.append(("k-held", held_done(st["session"], gid)))
    ops.append(("k-drop", {"operation": "delete", "table": "state",
                           "where": {"key": pending_key("gap-" + gid)}}))
    if st.get("engine") == "duplex" and not now_err and allowed(live, st.get("audience")):
        # A duplex call has no next round of this model to wait for: the voice
        # model is speaking now, so the find goes to it as a `fact` as well --
        # only when the round on the line now may see it (review M-10,
        # R2-I-14): the gap's round rode the ask out and home, and someone
        # may have joined the call since. Kept as an addendum all the same.
        return [lstore(ops, "kept", "gap-" + gid,
                       canonical({"fact": said_aloud(st["gap"], st["text"])}))]
    if st.get("engine") == "duplex" and now_err:
        sys.stderr.write("curator/push: gap %s: who is on the line could not be read (%s)"
                         " -- no fact, the addendum is kept\n" % (gid, now_err))
    elif st.get("engine") == "duplex":
        sys.stderr.write("curator/push: gap %s: the round on the line may not hear its find"
                         " -- no fact, the addendum is kept (GH #925)\n" % gid)
    return [lstore(ops, "done", "gap-" + gid)]


def held_done(session, gid):
    """The mark that lets a held find go (B6 c): once, whatever kept it."""
    value = canonical({"id": gid})
    return ins("marks", stamped({"seq": next_seq(1)[0], "session_id": session, "turn_id": "",
                                 "kind": "held_done", "value": value, "at": now()}, AUD),
               if_absent={"session_id": session, "kind": "held_done", "value": value})


if lane == "push_ask":
    ask = the_ask(hop, d)
    try:
        if not knob_on(hop.get("recall_push")):
            # GH #1044: a role without the push hands the question on as it
            # came, but its memory is sized by the same package as a pushed
            # one -- one read of `input_soft` (phase `pass`), nothing else.
            emit([lstore([("p-state", sel("state", ["key", "value"],
                                          {"key": "input_soft"}))],
                         "pass", str(uuid.uuid4()), canonical(ask))])
        budget = knob_budget(hop.get("recall_budget"))
        pid = str(uuid.uuid4())
        # The session as `./intake` keys it (R-KX-2): none named is "default".
        session = str(ask["header"].get("session_id") or "default")
        # GH #1225 B5: the ask rides `cur_reason` through both of its steps,
        # as phase `pass` carries its own: no state row holds it, so no read
        # can lose it, and a child started anew between the steps has it.
        stash = {"ask": ask, "budget": budget, "short": knob_on(hop.get("short_ids")),
                 "fixed": knob_on(hop.get("recall_budget_fixed"))}
        # The topic, the addenda, the wall page and the summary cover ask the
        # store for this round's rows only (GH #932): the page of `WALL_PAGE`
        # and the topic page fill with rows the round may see, and a hidden
        # row costs none of their places.
        # Every quiet turn leaves a nameless `continue` (the nothing form);
        # those carry nothing and would push a named mark out of the page.
        ops = round_read("a-topic", "marks", ["seq", "session_id", "value", "audience_set"],
                         {"session_id": session, "kind": "topic",
                          "value": {"neq": canonical({"movement": "continue", "name": ""})}},
                         [("seq", "desc")], 16, session)
        # The finds kept for this session and those held because their
        # marks could not be read (B6 c), in the same leg.
        ops += round_read("a-add", "marks", ["seq", "session_id", "turn_id", "kind", "value",
                                             "audience_set"],
                          {"session_id": session, "kind": {"in": ["addendum", "held"]}},
                          [("seq", "asc")], None, session)
        # Which finds were handed on is bookkeeping for a write (whether an
        # `addendum_done` is due), read whole: it only holds a visible find
        # back, and nothing of it leaves.
        ops.append(("a-done", sel("marks", ["seq", "kind", "value"],
                                  {"session_id": session,
                                   "kind": {"in": ["addendum_done", "held_done"]}},
                                  [("seq", "asc")])))
        ops += round_read("a-wall", "wall", ["seq", "session_id", "turn_id", "kind", "hash",
                                             "final", "audience_set"],
                          {"kind": {"in": ["user", "peer", "assistant"]}},
                          [("seq", "desc")], WALL_PAGE, session)
        ops += [("a-state", sel("state", ["key", "value"],
                                {"key": {"in": ["push:tier", "input_soft"]}})),
                ("a-slot", sel("slots", ["path", "hash", "owner"], {"path": HYGIENE_PATH}))]
        # The newest summary THIS round may see bounds its window; summaries
        # name no session, so a round-less ask reads none (cover 0).
        ops += round_read("a-cover", "summaries", ["covers_to_seq"], None,
                          [("covers_to_seq", "desc")], 1)
        # GH #949: the candidates this round may see ride the same bundle --
        # a leg more, never a round trip more; with `candidate_push` "0" not
        # even the leg.
        if CANDIDATE_PUSH:
            ops.append(("a-cand", sel("candidates", CANDIDATE_COLS, candidate_where(ROUND),
                                      [("priority", "desc"), ("at", "desc")], CANDIDATE_ROWS)))
        emit([lstore(ops, "ask", pid, canonical(stash))])
    except SystemExit:
        raise
    except Exception as exc:
        sys.stderr.write("curator/push: ask not enriched (%s) -- sent as it came\n" % exc)
        emit([ask])

if lane == "push_gap":
    # The splitter hands a string on as `{payload: <text>}`; a model that wrote
    # the section as an object gets its words read in order -- one gap, one
    # mark, whatever form it came in.
    payload = d.get("payload")
    if isinstance(payload, dict) and ("payload" in payload or "text" in payload):
        gap = payload.get("payload", payload.get("text", ""))
    elif isinstance(payload, dict):
        gap = " ".join(str(v) for v in payload.values() if isinstance(v, (str, int, float)))
    else:
        gap = payload
    gap = " ".join(str(gap or "").split())
    if not gap:
        park("a gap section without words -- nothing to look up")
    session = str(ctx.get("session_id") or hop.get("session_id") or "default")
    turn = str(ctx.get("turn_id") or hop.get("turn_id") or "")
    gid = hashlib.sha256(("%s\x1f%s\x1f%s" % (session, turn, gap)).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:16]
    # A1: whether this gap is on the record is the ledger's word -- its mark
    # is written if absent (phase `gap`) and only the message that wrote it
    # looks the gap up (phase `gap-m`); no RAM of this child decides it.
    info = {"id": gid, "text": gap, "engine": str(ctx.get("engine") or ""),
            "on": "1" if knob_on(hop.get("recall_push")) else "0",
            "budget": knob_budget(hop.get("recall_budget")),
            "fixed": "1" if knob_on(hop.get("recall_budget_fixed")) else "0",
            "iter": str(ctx.get("iter") or hop.get("iter") or "0")}
    emit([lstore([("g-state", sel("state", ["key", "value"],
                                  {"key": {"in": ["push:tier", "input_soft"]}}))],
                 "gap", gid, canonical(info))])

if lane == "in_gap_bundle":
    gid = str(ctx.get("gap_ask") or "")
    found = bundle_find(d, hop)
    if not gid:
        park("a gap bundle without its gap_ask -- dropped")
    if not found:
        park("gap %s: memory had nothing -- no addendum" % gid)
    session = str(ctx.get("session_id") or "default")
    pid = "gap-" + gid
    # A1: the find is put in one step by its key (a twin's answer replaces
    # it, never fails on `state_key`) and rides `cur_reason`; whether it is
    # kept already is the ledger's word (`h-marks`, then `k-mark` if absent).
    ops = [("h-put", ins("state", {"key": pending_key(pid), "value": canonical({"text": found})},
                         replace={"key": pending_key(pid)})),
           ("h-marks", sel("marks", ["turn_id", "kind", "value", "audience_set"],
                           {"session_id": session, "kind": {"in": ["gap", "addendum"]}}))]
    emit([lstore(ops, "hit", pid, canonical({"session": session, "text": found}))])

if lane:
    park("unknown lane %r -- dropped" % lane)

# ================================================================= PHASES
if not op:
    park("a message with neither a lane nor a store answer -- dropped")

lg = legs(d)

if phase == "done":
    report_errors(lg)
    release(call)
    emit(shown_of(carried(reason), lg) if reason else [])

if phase == "pass":
    # GH #1044: the untouched ask, home from its read of `input_soft`.
    ask = carried(reason)
    if not isinstance(ask.get("header"), dict):
        park("an ask handed on untouched lost its park -- dropped")
    report_errors(lg)
    soft = ""
    for r in rows(lg, "p-state"):
        if str(r.get("key") or "") == "input_soft":
            soft = str(r.get("value") or "")
    state_err = error_code_of(lg, "p-state")
    if state_err:
        soft = fallback_soft()
    emit([ask_as_it_came(ask, soft, ["p-state"] if state_err else [])])

if phase == "ask":
    # The ask is the one thing this phase must never lose: it rides
    # `cur_reason` (B5), so it leaves whatever the store answered.
    stash = carried(reason)
    ask = stash.get("ask")
    if not isinstance(ask, dict) or not isinstance(ask.get("header"), dict):
        park("ask %s carried no ask -- dropped" % call)
    soft = fallback_soft()
    failed = []
    try:
        report_errors(lg)
        head = ask["header"]
        # The session as the lane keyed its reads (R-KX-2).
        session = str(head.get("session_id") or "default")
        text = str(head.get("recall_query") or "")
        # GH #1225 B6: every read is asked whether it failed before its rows
        # are believed; the ask names what it was built without.
        topic_err = error_code_of(lg, "a-topic")
        wall_err = error_code_of(lg, "a-wall")
        add_err = error_code_of(lg, "a-add") or error_code_of(lg, "a-done")
        state_err = error_code_of(lg, "a-state")
        slot_err = error_code_of(lg, "a-slot")
        cover_err = error_code_of(lg, "a-cover")
        cand_err = error_code_of(lg, "a-cand")
        # OR-KF-35: a colony without the `candidates` table has no candidate --
        # the catalog code `unknown_table` is an empty read, never a degraded
        # one; every other failed leg (a timeout, a store error) stays degraded.
        if cand_err == "unknown_table":
            cand_err = ""
        failed = [cid for cid, e in (("a-topic", topic_err), ("a-wall", wall_err),
                                     ("a-add", add_err), ("a-state", state_err),
                                     ("a-slot", slot_err), ("a-cover", cover_err),
                                     ("a-cand", cand_err)) if e]
        # GH #925: the topic and the rows the entities come from are the ones
        # this round may be asked with -- a round that was not present when a
        # topic was named, or a row was said, is not asked with it.
        topics = [] if topic_err else visible(rows(lg, "a-topic"), session)
        topic = topic_of(topics)
        wall_rows = [] if wall_err else visible(rows(lg, "a-wall"), session)
        recent = recent_rounds(wall_rows)
        # Which finds were handed on is bookkeeping, read whole (`a-done`).
        # A failed read of either leaves every find waiting, unmarked (B6).
        pend, holds = [], []
        if not add_err:
            closed = {}
            for r in rows(lg, "a-done"):
                v = value_of(r)
                if isinstance(v, dict):
                    closed.setdefault(str(r.get("kind") or ""), set()).add(str(v.get("id") or ""))
            done = closed.get("addendum_done", set())
            kept = set()
            for r in rows(lg, "a-add"):
                v = value_of(r)
                if r.get("kind") != "addendum" or not isinstance(v, dict):
                    continue
                aid = str(v.get("id") or "")
                kept.add(aid)
                if not aid or aid in done or held("delivered", aid) or aid in [p["id"] for p in pend]:
                    continue
                # A find is handed only to a round the round of its gap holds; one
                # it does not stays, undone, for a later round that may see it.
                if not passes(r, ROUND, session):
                    continue
                pend.append({"id": aid, "call": str(v.get("call") or ""),
                             "result": str(v.get("result") or "")})
            for r in visible(rows(lg, "a-add"), session):
                v = value_of(r)
                gid = str(v.get("id") or "") if isinstance(v, dict) else ""
                if r.get("kind") == "held" and gid and gid not in kept \
                        and gid not in closed.get("held_done", set()) and gid not in holds:
                    holds.append(gid)
        covers = [] if cover_err else rows(lg, "a-cover")
        cover = int(covers[0].get("covers_to_seq") or 0) if covers else 0
        tier = {} if state_err else {str(r.get("key")): str(r.get("value") or "")
                                     for r in rows(lg, "a-state")}
        soft = fallback_soft() if state_err else tier.get("input_soft", "")
        slot = None if slot_err else (rows(lg, "a-slot") or [None])[0]
        refs = []
        for m in SHORT_ID.finditer(text):
            if m.group(1) not in refs:
                refs.append(m.group(1))
        refs = refs[:REF_MAX]
        # B4 (b): the spellings this round already knows as names -- the
        # topics the memory section named (the open one is asked with as the
        # topic) and the triggers of the candidates the round may see.
        known = []
        for r in topics:
            v = value_of(r)
            name = str(v.get("name") or "").strip() if isinstance(v, dict) else ""
            if name and name != topic and name not in known:
                known.append(name)
        # GH #949: which candidates this turn may carry is decided here, on
        # the person's words of this turn; their texts come with the blocks
        # below. A broken candidate costs the question nothing but itself.
        picked = []
        more = False
        if CANDIDATE_PUSH and not cand_err:
            try:
                found = rows(lg, "a-cand")
                more = len(found) >= CANDIDATE_ROWS
                if more:
                    sys.stderr.write("curator/push: ask %s read a full page of %d candidate "
                                     "rows (CANDIDATE_ROWS) -- more may exist\n"
                                     % (call, CANDIDATE_ROWS))
                for r in found:
                    if isinstance(r, dict) and candidate_passes(r, ROUND):
                        for t in triggers_of(r) or []:
                            if t.strip() and t.strip() not in known:
                                known.append(t.strip())
                picked = pick_candidates(found, ROUND, tokens_of(text), wall_rows,
                                         datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc),
                                         CANDIDATE_COOLDOWN)
            except Exception as exc:
                sys.stderr.write("curator/push: ask %s carries no candidate (%s)\n" % (call, exc))
                picked = []
        needed = sorted({str(r.get("hash") or "") for r in recent}
                        | {p["call"] for p in pend} | {p["result"] for p in pend}
                        | {c["hash"] for c in picked})
        slim = {"ask": ask, "budget": stash.get("budget", DEFAULT_BUDGET), "topic": topic,
                "short": bool(stash.get("short")), "fixed": bool(stash.get("fixed")),
                "input_soft": soft,
                "recent": [{"hash": str(r.get("hash") or ""), "kind": str(r.get("kind") or "")}
                           for r in recent],
                "pending": pend, "refs": refs, "known": known, "holds": holds,
                "failed": failed,
                "tier": tier.get("push:tier"), "has_tier": "push:tier" in tier,
                "tier_known": not state_err, "slot": slot, "slot_known": not slot_err}
        if picked:
            slim["cands"] = picked
            if more:
                slim["cands_more"] = CANDIDATE_ROWS
        ops = []
        if needed:
            ops.append(("b-blocks", sel("blocks", ["hash", "kind", "body"],
                                        {"hash": {"in": [h for h in needed if h]}})))
        if pend:
            # "In the window" is in the window of THIS round: a row it may not
            # see neither shows the pair nor keeps it back (GH #925).
            ops += round_read("b-seen", "wall", ["hash", "session_id", "audience_set"],
                              {"seq": {"gt": cover},
                               "hash": {"in": sorted({p["result"] for p in pend})}},
                              None, None, session)
        for i, ref in enumerate(refs):
            ops.append(("b-ref%d" % i, sel("blocks", ["hash", "body"], {"hash": {"gte": ref}},
                                           [("hash", "asc")], 1)))
            # The wall rows that carry the block, first in hash order: a short
            # id is resolved only where the round may see one of them -- an id
            # copied out of another conversation names nothing (GH #925). The
            # store hands back only rows the round may see (GH #932), so
            # `REF_ROWS` counts those alone.
            ops += round_read("b-refw%d" % i, "wall", ["hash", "session_id", "audience_set"],
                              {"hash": {"gte": ref}},
                              [("hash", "asc"), ("seq", "desc")], REF_ROWS, session)
        if not ops:
            # Nothing more to read: the second step runs here, no round trip.
            emit(finish_ask(slim, {}))
        emit([lstore(ops, "ask-b", call, canonical(slim))])
    except SystemExit:
        raise
    except Exception as exc:
        sys.stderr.write("curator/push: ask %s not enriched (%s) -- sent as it came\n"
                         % (call, exc))
        release(call)
        emit([ask_as_it_came(ask, soft, failed + ["enrich"])])

if phase == "ask-b":
    slim = carried(reason)
    ask = slim.get("ask")
    if not isinstance(ask, dict) or not isinstance(ask.get("header"), dict):
        park("ask %s carried no ask -- dropped" % call)
    try:
        report_errors(lg)
        emit(finish_ask(slim, lg))
    except SystemExit:
        raise
    except Exception as exc:
        sys.stderr.write("curator/push: ask %s not enriched (%s) -- sent as it came\n"
                         % (call, exc))
        release(call)
        emit([ask_as_it_came(ask, str(slim.get("input_soft") or ""),
                             list(slim.get("failed") or []) + ["enrich"])])

if phase == "gap":
    report_errors(lg)
    info = carried(reason)
    if not info.get("text"):
        park("gap %s lost what it asked -- dropped" % call)
    session = str(ctx.get("session_id") or hop.get("session_id") or "default")
    turn = str(ctx.get("turn_id") or hop.get("turn_id") or "")
    # B6: a failed read of the tier is no "this surface asks memory on no
    # turn": the gap is kept, marked as looked up without it, and said so.
    state_err = error_code_of(lg, "g-state")
    state = {} if state_err else {str(r.get("key")): str(r.get("value") or "")
                                  for r in rows(lg, "g-state")}
    tier = state.get("push:tier", "")
    searched = info.get("on") == "1" and bool(tier)
    value = {"id": call, "text": info.get("text", ""), "engine": info.get("engine", ""),
             "searched": 1 if searched else 0}
    if state_err:
        value["degraded"] = ["g-state"]
        sys.stderr.write("curator/push: gap %s: the tier could not be read (%s) -- kept,"
                         " not looked up\n" % (call, state_err))
    # The round of the answer that named the gap; it also rides the gap's own
    # ask out and its answer home, in the context. Written if absent (A1):
    # the one message whose write lands is the one that looks it up.
    # Keyed by the gap (its id, words and engine), not by what this message
    # read of the tier: a twin that read it otherwise is the same gap.
    keyed = {"session_id": session, "turn_id": turn, "kind": "gap", "value": canonical(value)}
    plain = {k: value[k] for k in ("id", "text", "engine")}
    forms = [canonical(dict(plain, searched=sr, **({"degraded": ["g-state"]} if dg else {})))
             for sr in (0, 1) for dg in (False, True)]
    mark = ins("marks", stamped(dict(keyed, seq=next_seq(1)[0], at=now()), AUD),
               if_absent=dict(keyed, value={"in": forms}))
    emit([lstore([("g-mark", mark)], "gap-m", call,
                 canonical(dict(info, tier=tier, soft=state.get("input_soft", ""),
                                searched=1 if searched else 0, quiet=1 if state_err else 0)))])

if phase == "gap-m":
    info = carried(reason)
    mark_err = error_code_of(lg, "g-mark")
    if mark_err:
        park("gap %s: its mark was not written (%s) -- not looked up" % (call, mark_err))
    if int((lg.get("g-mark") or {}).get("rows_affected") or 0) < 1:
        park("gap %s is already on the record -- not looked up twice" % call)
    if not info.get("searched"):
        if not info.get("quiet"):
            sys.stderr.write("curator/push: gap %s kept, not looked up (%s)\n"
                             % (call, "recall_push off" if info.get("on") != "1"
                                else "this surface asks memory on no turn"))
        emit([])
    # The second ask: the gap is its question, at the tier of this surface's
    # ambient leg, under the gap's own round -- and `gap_ask`, which the
    # parent's edge lifts into context so the answer finds its way back here
    # instead of into the collector. B7: the gap is asked WHOLE -- the
    # memory's own guard is the one place a question is cut (GH #88).
    session = str(ctx.get("session_id") or hop.get("session_id") or "default")
    turn = str(ctx.get("turn_id") or hop.get("turn_id") or "")
    head = {"route": "recall", "phase": "recall", "turn_id": turn, "session_id": session,
            "iter": str(info.get("iter") or "0"),
            "recall_query": str(info.get("text") or ""),
            "memory_tier": str(info.get("tier") or ""), "recall_window_from": "",
            "recall_window_to": "", "gap_ask": call}
    with_soft(head, str(info.get("soft") or ""))
    emit([{"header": head,
           "messages": [{"origin": "user", "type": "text", "text": head["recall_query"]}]}])

if phase == "hit":
    report_errors(lg)
    gid = call[len("gap-"):] if call.startswith("gap-") else call
    got = carried(reason)
    session = str(got.get("session") or "default")
    found = str(got.get("text") or "")
    # A held find (B6 c) comes back without its text: the state has it.
    echo_err = error_code_of(lg, "h-echo")
    if not found and not echo_err:
        echo = rows(lg, "h-echo")
        try:
            found = str(json.loads(str(echo[0].get("value") or "{}")).get("text") or "") if echo else ""
        except ValueError:
            found = ""
    marks_err = error_code_of(lg, "h-marks")
    if marks_err or echo_err:
        # B6 (c): whether the find is kept already cannot be told -- it is
        # HELD, never dropped: the state keeps it, a mark `held` names it,
        # and the next ask of its round looks at it again.
        ops = []
        if found:
            ops.append(("i-put", ins("state", {"key": pending_key(call),
                                               "value": canonical({"text": found})},
                                     replace={"key": pending_key(call)})))
        hv = canonical({"id": gid})
        ops.append(("i-held", ins("marks", stamped({
            "seq": next_seq(1)[0], "session_id": session, "turn_id": "", "kind": "held",
            "value": hv, "at": now()}, AUD), if_absent={"session_id": session, "kind": "held",
                                                       "value": hv})))
        sys.stderr.write("curator/push: gap %s: its marks could not be read (%s) -- the find"
                         " is held for the next message of its round\n"
                         % (gid, marks_err or echo_err))
        emit([lstore(ops, "done", call)])
    gap_row, known = None, False
    for r in rows(lg, "h-marks"):
        v = value_of(r)
        if not isinstance(v, dict) or str(v.get("id") or "") != gid:
            continue
        if r.get("kind") == "gap":
            gap_row = (r, v)
        elif r.get("kind") == "addendum":
            known = True
    if not found or gap_row is None or known:
        sys.stderr.write("curator/push: gap %s: %s -- no addendum\n"
                         % (gid, "its find is gone" if not found else
                            "no gap on the record" if gap_row is None else
                            "the addendum is already kept"))
        ops = [("i-drop", {"operation": "delete", "table": "state",
                           "where": {"key": pending_key(call)}})]
        if got.get("held"):
            ops.append(("i-done", held_done(session, gid)))
        emit([lstore(ops, "done", call)])
    r, v = gap_row
    gap = str(v.get("text") or "")
    c_el, r_el = addendum_pair(gap, found)
    # The addendum is made of two texts: the gap, said in the round of its
    # answer, and the find, looked up in the round this answer came home in --
    # the same round, which rode the gap's ask out and back in the context.
    # Its audience is the meet of both (OR-BD-3), never wider than either.
    # `h-marks` is read whole: a lookup by the gap's id for this write (the
    # gap's words, and whether the addendum is already kept). What it finds
    # leaves only inside the addendum, under the meet above (GH #932).
    st = {"gap": gap, "text": found, "turn": str(r.get("turn_id") or ""),
          "engine": str(v.get("engine") or ""), "session": session,
          "call": block_hash(c_el), "result": block_hash(r_el),
          "audience": addendum_audience(ROUND, r.get("audience_set")),
          "held": 1 if got.get("held") else 0}
    if st["engine"] != "duplex":
        emit(keep_find(st, gid, None))
    # The round on the line NOW: that of the session's newest call -- a
    # duplex find is spoken at once. Read whole on purpose (GH #932): it asks
    # WHO listens now, not what this round may see -- filtered by this round,
    # a newer call the round does not cover would hide behind an older one
    # and the find would be said to a round that may not hear it. Only
    # `allowed` reads it.
    emit([lstore([("j-now", sel("calls", ["audience_set"], {"session_id": session},
                                [("started_at", "desc")], 1))], "keep", call, canonical(st))])

if phase == "keep":
    report_errors(lg)
    gid = call[len("gap-"):] if call.startswith("gap-") else call
    st = carried(reason)
    if not st.get("text"):
        park("gap %s lost its find -- no addendum" % gid)
    # B6: who is on the line could not be read -- no fact (fail-closed).
    now_err = error_code_of(lg, "j-now")
    live = None if now_err else (rows(lg, "j-now") or [{}])[0].get("audience_set")
    emit(keep_find(st, gid, live, now_err))

if phase == "kept":
    # The fact of a duplex find, said only when THIS message kept it.
    report_errors(lg)
    gid = call[len("gap-"):] if call.startswith("gap-") else call
    mark_err = error_code_of(lg, "k-mark")
    if mark_err or int((lg.get("k-mark") or {}).get("rows_affected") or 0) < 1:
        park("gap %s: %s -- no fact" % (gid, "its addendum was not written (%s)" % mark_err
                                        if mark_err else "a twin kept it already"))
    fact = str(carried(reason).get("fact") or "")
    if not fact:
        park("gap %s lost its fact" % gid)
    emit([{"header": {"route": "sidecar", "section": "fact"}, "messages": [],
           "section": "fact", "payload": {"payload": fact}}])

park("store answer in unknown phase %r -- dropped" % phase)

candidate_cooldown.description: How many turns a candidate the push carried waits before it is carried again (GH #949): turns of the conversation the asking round saw since then, counted on the push's own page of the wall. 0 = no wait. A `once` candidate is carried once whatever this says.

candidate_push.description: Whether the push carries candidates at all (GH #949): "1" on, "0" off -- no ledger read, no pair, the push without them byte for byte. Null or empty is "1". The part takes a twentieth of the window this hive serves (state `input_soft`, R-IG-1) -- whole candidates, best first (priority, then the youngest), one that does not fit left out whole and said behind the part -- and every picked candidate when no window is known. Until curator 1.11 a fixed `candidate_budget` of 400 characters bounded it.

entity_max.description: At most this many names, dates, numbers and quotes the question of an ask carries in `mentioned:` (GH #1225 B8; R-27-11 A). 0 = none.

entity_rounds.description: The newest rounds of the wall whose words `mentioned:` is taken from (GH #1225 B8).

wall_page.description: The wall rows one ask reads for those rounds and for the candidates' cooldown (GH #1225 B8): the rows the round may see, newest first.

ref_max.description: At most this many short ids in the person's words are resolved into `refers to:` (GH #1225 B8).

ref_chars.description: The characters of a block a short id points at that `refers to:` carries; a longer block is cut with the mark `…` (GH #1225 B7/B8).

candidate_rows.description: The candidate rows one ask reads, best first (GH #949, GH #1225 B8); a full page is said on stderr and behind the part.

entity_stop_lang.description: The words of each language that are never a name -- salutations, pronouns, polite forms, articles, determiners, common nouns -- as `{"<lang>": [<word>, ...]}` (GH #1089, GH #1225 B4). A capital that is one of them is not taken into `mentioned:`. The German list is the one the memory hive reads (`entity_stop_lang.<lang>`). Absent: the English set of curator 1.11.

entity_det_lang.description: The words of `entity_stop_lang` a noun follows, per language (articles, possessives, determiners and their contractions; GH #1225 B4): a capital behind any other word of that list -- a salutation, a title, a kinship word -- is a name whatever its form ("Herrn Hartung", "Tochter Anna"); one behind a determiner gets no such pass and is not therefore a noun either -- German says "die Lotte" and "die Brille" alike, and only `entity_stop_lang` tells them apart.

entity_suffix_lang.description: Word endings of nouns, per language (GH #1225 B4): a capital that ends in one of them, with at least four letters in front of it, is a noun ("Entlastung", "Gesellschaft") -- the shorter stem keeps a name ("Dennis", "Jung").

entity_date_lang.description: The weekdays and months, per language (GH #1225 B4 (a)): a capital that is one of them is a date and taken into `mentioned:` wherever it stands ("im Mai", "jeden Sonntag").

entity_language.description: The languages of `entity_stop_lang` and `entity_det_lang` in use, comma-separated ("de,en"); empty is every language the lists carry -- a member may speak any of them, and nothing here guesses which (GH #1225 B4).

input_soft_fallback.description: The window an ask is sized by when the read of `input_soft` failed (GH #1225 B6): the `input_soft` of the catalogue row `input_soft_fallback_row` -- never the old sizes in silence. 0 = no fallback.

input_soft_fallback_row.description: The catalogue row `input_soft_fallback` is the window of (OR-IG-9): the model the talky is born on.

description.purpose: The recall push of one model (GH #895). It builds the question of the collector's per-turn memory ask out of the wall -- the topic the memory section last named in the session, what the last three rounds named, what a short id in the person's words points at -- in front of the person's own words and within `recall_budget`, and hands the ask on with exactly the collector's hop keys. It hands the model the push candidates `./intake` keeps for the round of the ask -- only those the round may see, still live, whose trigger the person's words of the turn say (or that have none), and not again within `candidate_cooldown` turns -- as ONE `memory_recall` pair whose result is their part within its share of the window (R-IG-1), what it left out said behind it, for `./intake` to write into the wall of that round ahead of its first turn; the question to the memory never carries them (GH #949). It looks a `gap` of an answer up after the answer, keeps a find as a `recall` pair and an `addendum` mark, and hands that pair to `./intake`, the wall's one writer, for the session's next round, ahead of its first turn; in a duplex call it also sends the find as a `fact` for the voice model.
description.use_when: Inside the curator only, behind `./policy`, which stamps the knobs `recall_push`, `recall_budget` and `short_ids` -- as the role resolved them -- on both of its doors.
description.not_in_scope: No model call and no retrieval of its own: memory answers, this cell only asks. An ask that cannot be enriched leaves as it came -- the collector's fan-in waits for it.
description.emits_meaning: recall: the ask, with the collector's keys (plus `gap_ask` on a gap's own ask). sidecar: a gap's find as a section `fact`, duplex calls only. lstore: ledger operations. in_addendum: the pairs of a round for `./intake`, which writes them into the wall of the round they open -- a gap's find, and the pair of the push candidates the turn carries (GH #949).
description.consumes_meaning: push_ask and push_gap from `./policy`, in_gap_bundle from outside (the answer to a gap's ask), and the ledger's answers to its phases (ask, ask-b, gap, hit, keep, done).
